_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: Bulk measured 2026-07-30 (run 30569500717). design-steel-thread.bats re-measured 2026-07-31 across four readings of shard 1/9 (122, 120, 121, 117) and lowered from 139 to their mean. lane-resolver / lane-surfaces / root-golden / shard-tests measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771) -- they had no entry at all and packed at _default_weight 16, which is the whole of the imbalance #69 shipped with: the packer balanced all nine shards to 132-139 predicted and the run came out 117-270, because lane-resolver.bats is 44 tests being counted as 16 seconds of work.
_known_gap: portability.bats grew in #71 and its 6 predates that. At 6 tests the error is worth ~15s against a 1585s total, so it is left rather than guessed at. arc-ci prints `shard-timing:` lines on every run; a shard that consistently overruns its prediction is how the next one of these gets caught.
